gaps.note: The outside work must be added, not subtracted: the paper's recurrence is F(e) <= (s/W)F(e/m) + O((eK)^tau+1) (paper.tex, Unrolling the recurrence, around line 2380). With a minus sign the bound is not the cost recurrence, and it contradicts the later sum of positive internal costs C f^lambda sum (...)^nu.

gaps.term: direction of the bound on lambda
gaps.quote: Taking $\lambda$ with $\lambda<\log_m(s/W)<1$ makes the ratio below 1
gaps.note: The ratio (s/W)/m^lambda is below 1 exactly when lambda > log_m(s/W), not <. The paper uses a<=m^sigma<m^lambda (a=s/W) with lambda>sigma>=log_m(s/W). The page's own example (lambda=0.8 > 0.585) and its later 'sigma < lambda' with sigma >= log_m(s/W) use the correct direction.

gaps.quote: and the leaves cost $O(f^\sigma d^{\vartheta(1-\sigma)})\le O(f^\lambda)$
gaps.note: Not true in general: leaves have f/m^nu < d^vartheta, and at f near d^vartheta the quantity f^sigma d^{vartheta(1-sigma)} is about f, which exceeds f^lambda. The paper (around lines 2400-2420) only gets O(e^sigma d^{beta(1-sigma)}) and carries it into the final bound d^{sigma+beta(1-sigma)} (hence lambda' > max{lambda, sigma+beta(1-sigma)}), not O(e^lambda).

gaps.quote: Each leaf is handled by one kernel per chunk, at cost $O(f/m^\nu)$.
gaps.note: The page never says what a kernel is (in the paper, the 2-input butterfly-like C map applied individually on one selected bit/chunk, costing O(V) each). The reader has no way to see why f/m^nu chunks cost O(f/m^nu) per unit volume.
